newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares advance on back of firmer dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares advance on back of firmer dollar.

text.p: German shares sought to keep up their heady gains on Tuesday with the help of the firmer dollar as the DAX index rose to another record high and resumed its uptrend after a pause on Monday, traders said.
The DAX index was up 48.47 points at 3,281.04 points in early bourse trade after reaching a new record high at 3,282.13 points, helped by the dollar climbing above 1.70 marks.
"The dollar is still the engine for the gains," said one Frankfurt trader.
But gains may be limited ahead of the afternoon when Wall Street resumes trading after the long U.S. holiday weekend.
And some traders said the market was still due for a period of consolidation after the recent heady gains in a bid to make the market appear attractive again to investors.

Bank stocks were a major factor pushing the market higher on Monday due to the positive reception of results from Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, and Vereinsbank, which both reported higher profits.
Deutsche was up 2.02 marks at 88.40 marks, while Vereinsbank was up 70 pfennigs at 64.60 marks.
Chemical shares were also in favour as BASF AG and Bayer AG both posted gains that outpaced the market.
Construction group Philipp Holzmann AG advanced nine marks to 460 marks after saying it expected 1996 construction output to be steady at 14.1 billion marks despite the weak economy.

Trading against the trend was carmaker Volkswagen AG, which fell 25 pfennigs to 806 marks after Monday's statement that production would be cut due to the Spanish trucker strike interrupting shipments from parts suppliers.

VW is also again under pressure after saying on Monday that it has asked German prosecutors to investigate allegations of purchasing department officials demanding and accepting bribes from supplier to be given contracts.
